display.title: Shmiras Halashon: Words Are Like Arrows
display.summary_short: Following the Chofetz Chaim, Uncle Yossi teaches that our words are like arrows: we control them before we speak, but once spoken they cannot be called back.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi introduces the Chofetz Chaim, the great rabbi named after his famous sefer on shmiras halashon, and his teaching that a person's very life depends on his tongue: words can bring good fortune, or, if we are careless, great harm. Following the Baal Shem Tov's instruction to learn a lesson in serving Hashem from everything we see, he describes a bow and arrow. While the arrow is still on the string, the archer decides when and where to shoot, but once it flies he cannot stop it or change its course. Words are the same: before we speak we can choose the right words and tone, but afterwards it is too late. That is why, our Sages say, Hashem placed the tongue behind two walls, the teeth and the lips, to show how carefully it must be guarded.
display.lesson: Think before you speak, because words, like arrows, cannot be taken back.
